🧪 **F-2597-1 — AN ENUMERATION IN A LAW SURFACE CERTIFIES THE MEMBERS IT DID NOT COUNT: RT-01's "THREE other guard consumers" IS FOUR, AND THE UNCOUNTED ONE IS THE ONLY ONE THAT PINS A ROTATION ID AS A HARDCODED LITERAL (fire s2597, dry board, 65th consecutive).** ✅ **THE VERDICT FIRST, SO THE CORRECTION IS NOT MISREAD AS AN ALARM: the Monday `r2026w39` mint is SAFE, and that is MEASURED rather than argued — a scratch mint into a COPY of the registry (never the tracked file, 3 days before the trigger) leaves `rotations[0]` **BYTE-IDENTICAL**, so all four `rotations[0]` consumers are append-safe and a mint changes nothing for any of them.** 📊 **MEASURED s2597 by RE-SWEEPING the consumers instead of inheriting the list: `bench-seeds.test.mjs:124` · `review-party-retention.test.mjs:14` · `test-standings.mjs:1189` — the three the law names — **plus `e2e/transfer-board.spec.ts`, which it does not**, importing the registry at `:4` and keying on `rotations[0]` at `:20` and `:32`.** 🔑 **AND THE FOURTH IS QUALITATIVELY DIFFERENT, WHICH IS WHY IT IS THE ONE WORTH FINDING: at `:31` it asserts `toContainText('r2026w37 closes')` — a HARDCODED id literal, NOT derived from `rotations[0].id`. It agrees with its derived sibling at `:32` ONLY because the registry is APPEND-ONLY (`rotation-mint.mjs:52-53` filters the same id, concats, sorts by `opensAt`, so a new rotation always sorts LAST and `rotations[0]` is frozen). **That convention is load-bearing for a string literal and was written down nowhere.** The day anyone PRUNES the oldest rotation, `:31` breaks LOUD on a stale literal while `:32` SILENTLY FOLLOWS the new `rotations[0]` — one fails, one changes subject.** ⚖️ **SEVERITY STATED HONESTLY AND DELIBERATELY NOT INFLATED: realised cost ZERO, nothing is broken, NOT a false green, no mint was ever wrong, and nothing is owed before Monday. This corrects an ENUMERATION, not a verdict.** 🎯 **What earns it a row is WHO READS THE COUNT AND WHEN: that clause exists so a fire can budget a mint's blast radius, and it hands that fire a NUMBER — so a fire checking "the three consumers" stops at three and never opens the one file whose coupling is a literal. F-2358-1 exactly: *a guard enumerating one member of a class certifies the uncovered members as clean* — here it is a LAW enumerating three of four.** 🖨️ **A SECOND, USABLE FACT BANKED AT THE SITE: the fence body is **BYTE-IDENTICAL** to `JSON.stringify(registry, null, 2)` (30 lines, compared EQUAL and not merely `deepEqual`), so RT-01 step 2 is a REGENERATION, not a hand-paste — and hand-pasting 30 lines into 43 is precisely the step that can silently drop a rotation and re-create the defect F-2594-1 cured.** 🔢 **s2595's EXPLICIT RE-VERIFY INSTRUCTION IS DISCHARGED, AND STRUCTURALLY RATHER THAN BY LUCK: the SOLE law pointer into `public/skill.md` is `:367` (measured — 74 baseline sources, exactly one targets that file) and the fence spans `371–404`, so the pointer sits 4 lines ABOVE a block that grows DOWNWARD. Measured growth **+13 lines per rotation** (371–404 today → 371–417 after the mint). No law pointer rots on a mint; `0` baseline pointers target `scripts/fire.md` at all.** 📈 **ONE DATED, COMPOUNDING CONSEQUENCE NAMED SO IT IS NOT DISCOVERED LATE: +13 lines/week forever is ~700 lines of JSON a year on `public/skill.md`, a RIDER-FACING page. Nothing owed today — recorded because the trim that eventually follows is exactly the act that breaks `:31` above.** 🚫 **NO GUARD, and the restraint is INHERITED rather than re-argued: "does this prose still enumerate its class completely?" is a judgement over free text, so a red fires on every honest sentence and is excused into uselessness inside a week (F-1460-1, the `cross-engine` fate) — the same restraint F-2450-1 took for a live instruction and F-2595-1 took for this very duty. The cure is the amended clause in `scripts/fire.md`.** 💡 **REUSABLE, and it is the RUNG UNDER s2595's lesson: that finding said a dated duty accumulates verified FACTS and unverified VERBS, so TYPE THE STEPS.
